function: A3C-based DRL jointly sets each secondary UAV's sensing/communication bandwidth and power split, plus CPU computing capacity of secondary and central UAVs (p. 7).
system: Central UAV plus four secondary UAVs with antenna arrays (sensing and communication beams, OFDM), 15 vehicles, 5 MHz bandwidth, carrier frequency not stated, no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: A3C actor-critic deep reinforcement learning; CU global network updated by averaging worker gradients (FedAvg), centralized training, distributed execution; MLPs 128x256x128 (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: 1000x1000 m Manhattan block, 15 Poisson vehicles; air-to-air log-distance path loss with parameters from measurement-based model [21]; radar echo model; no dataset (pp. 5, 10).
test_conditions: Up to 1500 training episodes of 500 steps (K=15 vehicles, 4 SUs, 1-3 Mb data); ten test episodes; data volume, SU count, weights varied in further runs (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Learned: PPO, REINFORCE, DDPG. Non-learned: PSO, Greedy (equal split, maximum computing), Random (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Reward, ISCC success rate, energy consumption, energy efficiency, processing latency, runtime per episode (pp. 11-12, Table III).
complexity: Order O(Te Ts (sum la(i)la(i+1) + sum lc(i)lc(i+1))) in episodes, steps, layer units (p. 10); runtime per episode: MCAI 1.015 s, PSO 148.301 s (Table III, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 5: "the logarithmic distance path loss model in [21]". Custom simulator with a log-distance air-to-air path loss (parameters in Table II, p. 10) and a radar echo model (p. 4); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is used for training or testing.
q2_support: p. 12: "the REINFORCE algorithm fails to learn an effective policy when the data volume is between 2 and 4 Mb". Data volume, SU count and weights are varied as separate learning outcomes (pp. 12-13); no trained policy is stated to be tested on conditions unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 11: "the success rates of MCAI, PPO, and PSO are all greater than 99%". Learned baselines PPO, REINFORCE, DDPG (pp. 10-11) and non-learned PSO, Greedy, Random (p. 11) are compared on reward, success rate and energy efficiency (Table III, p. 12).
q4_support: p. 10: "computational complexity can be represented as" an order O(Te Ts (sum la(i)la(i+1) + sum lc(i)lc(i+1))) (Eq. 56); runtime per episode in Table III (p. 12) and Table V (p. 13).
q5_support: p. 10: "parallel computing toolbox available in MATLAB 2023b to construct and train the DRL agent". Own MATLAB simulation; no code or data link, no public dataset, no measured data.
notes: Areas 5 and 6 both fit (bandwidth and power split between sensing and communication in a UAV network); area 6 taken by the tie-break order, reviewer to confirm. The CPU capacity control is above the physical layer, but the work learns physical-layer resource allocation jointly with it, so above_phy does not apply. The air-to-air path-loss parameters come from the measurement-based model of [21], yet no measured data is used for training or testing, so q1 is 0. The paper does not say whether the agents were retrained for each data volume or SU count (M changes the state and action sizes), hence q2 is 0; reviewer to confirm. Tables II to VI read from the page images (pp. 10, 12, 13).
